english.html: kinds of Magic: as when Demaenetus of Parrhasia (or, if you will believe Pausanias <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>, Demarchus), having tasted of the sacrifice of a young child which the Arcadians made to Lycaeus their God, was turned into a wolf, and at the end of ten years took again the form of a man <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>. Whereof St Augustine learnedly disputes <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>, and shows these things to be no less fabulous than what is written of the companions of Diomedes, King of Aetolia, who after the destruction of Troy were transmuted into birds; and of Circe, who is feigned to have transmuted Scylla (of whom she was jealous) into a sea-monster, and the companions of Ulysses into swine.

notes.citation: Pausanias, Description of Greece, the Eliaca (book VI, 6.8.2: Damarchus of Parrhasia, the Olympic boxer said to have turned into a wolf at the sacrifice to Zeus Lycaeus and back again in the tenth year)
notes.gloss: Pausanias himself does not believe it.

notes.citation: Pliny, Natural History VIII.22 (§§81–82 in the modern numbering, VIII.34): Demaenetus of Parrhasia, from Scopas
notes.original: Pline au li. viij. c. xxij.
notes.gloss: Pliny: having tasted the entrails of a boy sacrificed by the Arcadians to Jupiter Lycaeus, he became a wolf and returned to human shape in the tenth year, and won at boxing at Olympia.

notes.citation: Augustine, City of God XVIII.17–18 (printed "the eighth": the discussion of the Arcadian wolves, Diomedes's companions and Circe is in book XVIII, chapters 16–18)
notes.gloss: Augustine denies that demons can change the substance of a body and explains such transformations as phantasms impressed on the senses.
Carminibus Circe socios mutavit Ulixi; the line follows the one at {h} in Virgil. Translated in the text with the Latin in parentheses.

english.html: With her charms Circe transformed the companions of Ulysses (Carminibus Circe socios mutavit Ulixis) n.

notes.gloss: The citation serves the verse just given.

english.html: Among such prodigies we approve only the history of Nebuchadnezzar, King of Babylon, who by the will of God was transmuted into an ox, and remained so seven years among the other beasts, eating grass; and afterwards, by the mercy of God, the figure of a man was restored to him <sup class="mk" data-key="o">o</sup>. Not that I would altogether deny the conversion among human beings from one sex to the other: for besides the examples recounted by Pliny and Gellius <sup class="mk" data-key="p">p</sup>, there is reason plain enough that this can be done without Magic or any artifice; for man and woman have the instruments for begetting altogether alike, save that the man's extends outward and the woman's inward, and that the testicles (or, if you prefer, the genitories) do not hang in women. Nothing is needed, then, to bring about the said conversion, but that by some accident of sickness, or otherwise, the man's member withdraw within the body, and he will become a woman; or that the woman's advance outward, and behold a man <sup class="mk" data-key="q">q</sup>. True it is that I do not remember ever to have read an example of a man being transmuted into a woman, but only of women, that they are sometimes transformed into men: wherein nature shows her clemency and benignity, in not willing to change things for the worse, but always for the better. There are several other kinds of Magic, which there is no need to write of here, especial

notes.citation: Daniel 4 (4:25–34, Vulgate 4:22–34): Nebuchadnezzar driven from men to eat grass as the oxen for seven times, and restored
notes.gloss: Coras's tranſmué en bœuf reads the text as a bodily transformation, which the passage does not literally say; translated as he wrote it.

notes.citation: Pliny, Natural History VII.4 (§§34–36: women changed into men — the Casinum girl, Lucius Constitius of Thysdrus, Arescon of Argos); Aulus Gellius (Aule Gelle), Attic Nights IX.4 (§§13–16, citing Pliny's examples)
notes.original: Pline liure vij. c. iiij. Aule Gelle liure ix. c. iiij.
notes.gloss: Pliny: gignere mares feminas non est fabulosum, and he had himself seen a man so changed in Africa.

notes.citation: Galeotto Marzio of Narni (Galeotus Mar.), De doctrina promiscua, ch. 23 (as cited; chapter unverified)
notes.original: Galeotus Mar. au liure de doctrina promiſcua c. xxiij.
notes.gloss: Galeotto Marzio, c. 1427–c. 1497; the De doctrina promiscua (printed 1548) treats medical and astrological curiosities, among them the change of sex, in the humoral terms Coras repeats.

(ou ſi tu veux croire à Pauſanias {k}) Demarchus: ayant
gouſté du ſacrifice, que les Arcades faiſoyent à Lycee
leur Dieu d'vn ieune enfant, fut conuerti en loup: & au
bout de dix ans reprint la forme d'homme {l}. Dequoy
S. Auguſtin diſpute doctement {m}, & monſtre ces cho-
ſes n'eſtre pas moins fabuleuſes, que ce qu'on eſcrit des
compagnõs de Diomedes Roy d'Aetolie, leſques apres
la deſtruction de Troye furent tranſmuez en oyſeaux:
& de Circé, laquelle on feint auoir tranſmué Scilla
(de qui elle eſtoit ialouſe) en vn monſtre marin: & les
compagnons d'Vliſſes en porceaux.
Carminibus Circe, ſocios mutauit Vliſsis {n}.
En tels prodiges nous approuuons ſeulement l'hi-
ſtoire de Nabuchodonoſor Roy de Babylone, qui par
la volonté de Dieu fut tranſmué en bœuf, & demeura
ainſi ſept ans parmi les autres beſtes, mangeant l'herbe:
& apres par la miſericorde de Dieu, la figure d'homme
luy fut rendue {o}. Non que ie vueille du tout nier la cõ-
uerſion entre les hommes d'vn ſexe en autre: car outre
les exemples recitez par Pline, & Gelle {p}, il y a raiſon
aſſez apparente, que cela ſe puiſſe faire ſans Magie, ou
aucun artifice: car l'homme & la femme ont les in-
ſtrumens pour engendrer du tout ſemblabes: hors
mis que celuy de l'homme ſ'eſtend par dehors: & ce-
luy de la femme par dedans, & que les teſticules (ou
ſi mieux aimez, genitoires) ne pendent point aux fem
mes. Il ne faut donc pour faire ladite conuerſion, ſi-
non, que par quelque accident de maladie, ou autre-
ment, le membre de l'homme ſe retire dedans le corps,
& il deuiendra femme: ou que celuy de la femme ſ'a-
uance par dehors, & voila vn homme {q}. Vray eſt qu'il
ne me ſouuient point d'auoir oncques léu exemple
qu'vn homme ſe tranſmuaſt en femme: mais ſeulement
des femmes, qu'elles ſe transforment quelquesfois en
hommes: enquoy nature monſtre ſa clemence & be-
nignité, de ne vouloir point changer les choſes en pis:
mais touſiours en meilleur. Il y a pluſieurs autres eſ-
